question: Young sunflowers follow the sun across the sky, but once they bloom, most stop moving and face one fixed direction all day. Which compass direction?
topic: Plants and trees that break the rules
source_excerpt: Young sunflower plants track the Sun from east to west during the day and then reorient during the night to face east in anticipation of dawn. In contrast, mature plants cease movement with their flower heads facing east.

extra.why_interesting: Everyone 'knows' sunflowers follow the sun all day. In fact grown flowers freeze in place, and a player can reason out which way they face by asking which sun would matter most to a cold flower in the morning.
extra.verification_notes: Atamian et al. 2016 (Science) found mature sunflowers cease movement with flower heads facing east; I found no later work contradicting it. https://harmerlab.plantclock.org/papers/Atamian-Science

explanation: Facing the rising sun warms the flower head early in the morning, and warm flowers attract far more bees than cold ones.

question: Orchids are usually grown just to look at, but one of them gives us a flavour found in ice cream, cakes and cola. Which flavour comes from the dried seed pod of an orchid?
topic: Plants and trees that break the rules
source_excerpt: Vanilla, orchid genus whose fruits, called vanilla beans, are cured and used as a flavouring.

extra.why_interesting: People think of orchids as flowers to look at, not to eat. One of the world's most familiar flavours actually comes from an orchid, and the 'orchid' and 'pod' clues are enough for most players to get there.
extra.verification_notes: Vanilla is derived from the cured fruit pods of Vanilla orchids (e.g. V. planifolia); no newer development affects this, per Britannica.

explanation: Vanilla comes from a climbing orchid. Outside its native Mexico, almost every flower has to be pollinated by hand, which is why real vanilla is so expensive.
